data.name: ATP-competitive mTOR inhibitors
data.description: Torin1, AZD8055 and relatives occupy the mTOR active site directly, inhibiting both complexes.
data.description_beginner: Drugs that block mTOR's engine instead of getting in its way.

studies.title: Active-site inhibitors of mTOR target rapamycin-resistant outputs of mTORC1 and mTORC2
studies.authors: Feldman ME; Apsel B; Uotila A; Loewith R; Knight ZA; Ruggero D; Shokat KM

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: The parallel discovery to Thoreen 2009 (same year), from the Shokat lab. Their TORKinibs (PP242, PP30) block mTOR's active site, hitting both complexes and shutting down cap-dependent translation that rapamycin misses. Together these two papers established a whole new drug class beyond rapamycin.

studies.title: An ATP-competitive mammalian target of rapamycin inhibitor reveals rapamycin-resistant functions of mTORC1
studies.authors: Thoreen CC; Kang SA; Chang JW; Liu Q; Zhang Jianming; Gao Y; Reichling LJ; Sim T; Sabatini DM; Gray NS

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: Dropped a bombshell: rapamycin does NOT fully block mTORC1. Using Torin1 (which jams the active site directly), the authors showed rapamycin leaves important mTORC1 jobs running - notably 4E-BP1 phosphorylation and autophagy suppression. This reframed a decade of rapamycin experiments and launched the search for complete inhibitors.

studies.title: AZD8055 is a potent, selective, and orally bioavailable ATP-competitive mammalian target of rapamycin kinase inhibitor with in vitro and in vivo antitumor activity
studies.authors: Chresta CM; Pass M et al.

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: AZD8055, an ATP-competitive mTOR kinase inhibitor, blocks both mTORC1 and mTORC2 (rapamycin-resistant outputs).

relations.mechanism: Occupies the mTOR active site in competition with ATP, so inhibition does not depend on obstructing substrate access and is not partial in the way rapalog inhibition is.
relations.boundary: Cell-line pharmacology. Clinical development of this class has been limited by toxicity attributed to simultaneous mTORC2 inhibition, which is precisely what the bi-steric design tries to avoid.

relations.mechanism: The same active site is present in both complexes, so an ATP-competitive inhibitor cannot distinguish them.
relations.boundary: Explains the metabolic and immunological toxicity of this class relative to rapalogs; the magnitude in patients is not established from these cell-line studies.
